editorial:
Ever wondered what it would be like to see a legendary book brought to life with clay? You get to follow a delusional but sweet old man who thinks he is a brave knight in a world that is definitely not a fairy tale. Along with his funny sidekick, Sancho Panza, he goes on wild adventures to save people who do not actually need saving. The whole vibe is quirky and colorful, making the old story feel fresh and easy to follow without feeling like a boring school assignment.

You will probably love how the clay figures move and the funny ways they react to the world around them. The pacing is steady, though some parts might feel a bit slow if you are looking for non-stop action. It is a great pick for families or anyone who likes unique art styles.
endingExplained: In the end, the main character finally wakes up from his fantasy. He realizes that the giants were just windmills and his quests were not real. He finds peace and accepts who he truly is before he passes away quietly. It is a sad but sweet wrap-up that shows how his imagination gave him joy, even if the rest of the world thought he was just crazy.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stop-motion art and classic stories.
